title: Kirishi burns, Abu Dhabi talks loom, and the Roosevelt reaches Singapore
summary: Ukrainian drones set Russia's Kirishi refinery ablaze while Russian strikes kill three in Odesa, the Komyshuvakha toll rises to fifty-five, the Kremlin rejects a European role in Tuesday's Abu Dhabi talks, Trump calls new Iran strikes highly unlikely as Rubio and Tehran trade barbs, Saudi Arabia details the missile attack on Riyadh, and the Theodore Roosevelt docks in Singapore on its way to the Middle East.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Monday, November ninth. We're one day out from the next round of Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, and both sides spent the weekend hitting each other hard.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's start there. Overnight, Ukrainian drones set fire to the Kirishi refinery in Russia's Leningrad region. That's Russia's second-largest refinery.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The regional governor, Aleksandr Drozdenko, says the fire has been contained. He says one woman was killed by falling drone debris, and that air defences downed a hundred and thirteen Ukrainian drones.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And Russia's attack on Ukraine was even bigger. Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched three hundred and seventeen long-range drones overnight, a hundred and five of them jet-powered, plus cruise missiles.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Odesa, the head of the city's military administration says three people were killed. And regional authorities say twenty-eight people were injured across Ukraine over the past day, with energy facilities hit in several regions.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's after a weekend of strikes on the grid. Yesterday we talked about more than six hundred thousand people losing power in the Dnipropetrovsk region. In its latest assessment, the Institute for the Study of War described a second straight night of Russian strikes on energy and critical infrastructure.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: There's also a grim update from Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region. That's where Russian guided bombs hit a school used as an aid centre on November second.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The Associated Press now puts the death toll from that strike at at least fifty-five. And on Sunday, it reports, a Russian drone hit emergency workers responding at the same site.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Ukraine has accused Russia before of striking the same place twice, to hit the crews who come to help. Russia has said it was targeting Ukrainian military units in the original strike.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the ground, the Institute for the Study of War says Russian forces attacked near Kostiantynivka, east of Sloviansk, toward Kupiansk and near Orikhiv on Sunday, without confirmed gains.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The exception is Dobropillia. The Institute assessed that Russian forces recently advanced, or infiltrated positions, in and around that town.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Now, the diplomacy. The US, Russia and Ukraine meet again in Abu Dhabi tomorrow, Tuesday. And there's already a fight over who's in the room.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: France says European officials will attend. An EU official told NPR that security officials from the bloc, NATO, France, Germany and Britain would be there, though it's not clear how they'd take part.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The Kremlin says Europeans will not take part. Vladimir Medinsky will lead Russia's delegation again, and the US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due in Abu Dhabi on the tenth and eleventh.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So the big question for Tuesday is whether those talks even start with everyone at the table.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's turn to Iran. On Sunday, President Trump said renewed strikes were highly unlikely to be needed if Iran signs what he called a very strong agreement. But he said he would authorize them if necessary.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Secretary of State Marco Rubio was more downbeat. He said the talks had not been productive, and that some of Iran's demands were, quote, outrageous and ridiculous, and not realistic.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Iran pushed back today. Its Foreign Ministry defended an offer to restart talks within two days, calling it the most reasonable proposal on the table.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And its spokesman asked whether it's unreasonable for Iran to want US sanctions and the naval blockade lifted before negotiations start. That's really the core of the dispute.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Meanwhile, there's more detail on Saturday's shipping incidents near the strait. The British maritime agency UKMTO said a tanker caught fire about eight nautical miles northwest of Khasab, in Oman, and its crew abandoned ship.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: About an hour later, another tanker heading out through the strait was hit by an unknown projectile. All its crew were safe. Open-source analysts have tentatively named the burning ship as the Navig8 Messi, but that hasn't been confirmed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And Iran's Revolutionary Guards still say ships are hitting mines on unauthorized routes. UKMTO hasn't confirmed the cause of any of these fires.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now to the Houthis and Saudi Arabia. We have a fuller picture of Sunday's attack on Riyadh.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Saudi air defences say they intercepted three ballistic missiles, two cruise missiles and a drone, most of them aimed at Riyadh. Debris damaged an Aramco building in the financial district, and the Energy Ministry says no one was hurt.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The Houthis say they're retaliating for Saudi airstrikes on areas they hold. None of the casualty claims on either side have been independently verified.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: A few more stories from the map. In southern Lebanon, Middle East Eye reported Israeli strikes on al-Tayri, in the Bint Jbeil district, on Friday. That adds to the shelling and demolitions we've covered there all week.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Sudan, Sudan Tribune reports the army and its allies took the town of Iyal Bakhit in West Kordofan on Saturday, and shot down long-range drones from the Rapid Support Forces. Those claims haven't been independently confirmed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And around Taiwan, the defence ministry reported four Chinese military aircraft sorties and six navy ships in twenty-four hours. The Taipei Times reports analysts think a large Chinese naval and coast guard presence in the western Pacific may be rehearsing how to isolate the island.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Finally, the ships. This is the one move on the map today. The carrier Theodore Roosevelt pulled into Changi Naval Base in Singapore on Friday, along with two of its escorts, according to USNI News.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: It's expected to head to the Middle East and relieve the George Washington, which is in the Arabian Sea alongside the George H. W. Bush. A US official told Axios the Roosevelt won't enter Central Command's area before mid-November.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: There are unconfirmed reports today that it has already left Singapore heading west. We'll update the map once that's confirmed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. Tuesday's talks in Abu Dhabi, and whether Europe ends up in the room. Whether the US and Iran find a way back to negotiating. And when the Roosevelt reaches the Arabian Sea, which could briefly give the region three carriers.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
